netOne.title: Full Stack Web Developer
netOne.description:
Developed ERP functionalities, migrating legacy modules from pure Java to a modern architecture using Spring Boot, Angular, and MySQL.
Cut a bulk document-processing job from ~10 minutes to under 1 minute, by reworking its database access and then processing the documents in parallel batches with Java 21 virtual threads.
Optimized SQL queries and core algorithms, achieving significant improvements in performance and scalability.
Built a public REST API with JWT, documented using OpenAPI/Swagger.
Consumed external marketplace and payment APIs (MercadoLibre, Mercado Pago, Tiendanube).
Worked across both frontend and backend, applying Clean Code principles and maintaining high-quality documentation.
Managed tasks independently, leading the full development cycle from analysis to delivery.
Tested with JUnit 5 and Mockito.

about.title: About Me
about.paragraph: I'm Nicolás Martín Catania, a developer from Argentina and Software Engineering student, currently working as a full stack developer at NetOne. Beyond my enthusiasm for tech, I enjoy playing the guitar, going to the gym, learning new languages and continuously learning and improving.

projectsInfo.title: Projects
projectsInfo.subtitle: Things I built to learn something, to solve a problem, or both. Filter by stack.

project1.name: MySongSet
project1.desc: Web application for organizing songs that I play on the guitar in playlists, using Spotify API integration and a minimalistic UI design. It helped me to not forget about the songs that I know, because I always end up playing the same 10 over and over.

project2.name: Basic products API
project2.desc: API featuring CRUD of different entities such as products and users, user roles, Spring Security, and JWT auth. Includes a basic frontend.

project3.name: Battle simulation in Java
project3.desc: Final project developed in a group for an advanced programming subject. Console application built in Java using many design patterns, with a small connection to Prolog. Simulates a turn-based battle between wizards and Death Eaters.

project4.name: BudgetKing
project4.desc: Financial tracker web application designed for personal use and learning purposes, built with Java, Spring, Angular, and a containerized MySQL database. Tracks income and expenses, groups them by category and spending accounts, and filters data by date with summary dashboards. Implements basic CI/CD and layered unit & integration tests.

project5.name: URL Shortener
project5.desc: Microservices-based URL shortener with hexagonal architecture. Uses RabbitMQ to handle messages and event transmission between microservices, and performs asynchronous email sending when users register. Includes logging and Testcontainers for integration testing. Uses k6 for stress testing. In development.

project6.name: Resilience & Observability Demo
project6.desc: Spring Boot example demonstrating resilience patterns with Resilience4j and observability using HTTP client.

project7.name: The Runner
project7.desc: Virtual threads practice with Spring Boot 4.0.2, using configuration classes to inject executor service.

project8.name: Simple Gym Modulith
project8.desc: Learning project bridging monolith and microservices using Spring Modulith, enforcing domain boundaries and event-driven architecture.

project9.name: The Testcontainers
project9.desc: Learning about Testcontainers integration in Spring Boot 4.0.2.
